intro_html: Enchilada night, minus the rolling and the oven time, all in one pan. These bowls hit a serious 52 grams of protein each and come in around $6.62 a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one skillet means the whole week is covered.
cost_closing_html: About $6.62 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls packs 52 grams of protein and about 566 calories.
upsell_html: Big Tex-Mex flavor with 52 grams of protein a bowl, and it reheats like a champ. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Buy your black beans by the case of store-brand cans. They are the cheap workhorse that stretches the beef.
A single bag of shredded cheddar is plenty for the whole batch, so no need to overbuy.
Chili powder and cumin last for months, so buy one jar of each and reuse them across dozens of batches.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, then drain off the grease.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin and let them bloom in the hot beef for a minute.
Add the enchilada sauce and corn and simmer until it thickens up a bit.
Fold in the seasoned black beans and warm everything through.
Spoon it into bowls over the beans, then top with shredded cheddar so it melts in.
